title: Vaccination Rates and Family Barriers Among Children with Inflammatory Bowel Disease.
ehr_evidence: Indiana utilizes an online registry, the Children and Hoosier Immunization Program (CHIRP), which was used by research assistants to access vaccination records for each participant.
summary: Cross-sectional study comparing vaccination rates and parental attitudes toward vaccine safety and effectiveness between children with IBD and non-IBD controls.
key_findings: IBD families reported higher concern about vaccine safety (40% vs 16%, P=0.03) and effectiveness (34% vs 12%, P<0.01) compared to non-IBD families.
36% of IBD families worried vaccines would worsen their child's symptoms vs 10% of non-IBD (P≤0.01).
96% of IBD children on biologics were missing the PPSV23 booster.
51% of IBD children were missing at least one HPV-9 vaccine or had never received one.
56% of IBD children were missing an influenza vaccine from the 2018-2019 season.
0% of IBD children were missing HBV vaccines compared to 11% of non-IBD (P=0.022).
14% of IBD parents changed their vaccine opinion after diagnosis vs 3% of non-IBD parents (P=0.06).
captured_features: clinical data (IBD type, medications, surgery history)
population: Children aged 10–25 years with IBD (n=50) and non-IBD GI controls (n=58) from a tertiary children's hospital in Indianapolis, IN
limitations: small sample size and convenience sampling
control group consisted of non-IBD GI clinic patients rather than healthy controls
CHIRP registry data may miss early childhood vaccinations due to 2015 mandate start date
demographically homogenous cohort (mostly white, high education)
data_availability_statement: Data stored and supported on figshare.com at https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.12442757.v1.
